newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ's Bolger says second break-up of ECNZ likely.
newsitem.headline: NZ's Bolger says second break-up of ECNZ likely.

text.p: New Zealand Prime Minister Jim Bolger predicted on Thursday that a wave of electricity sector reform, signalled earlier today in the budget, was set to lead to another break-up of state-owned power generator ECNZ.
"In the electricity industry there will be a further shake-up, almost certainly a further split of ECNZ," Bolger told reporters at a post-budget news conference.
Ministers had earlier announced a review of the electricity industry and the generation sector aimed at ensuring competition in the new wholesale market, launched on October 1 last year.
They declined to specify what plans they had in mind for ECNZ.
In June 1995, Contact Energy was split off from ECNZ with 29 percent of the country's generation capacity, and controls were placed on ECNZ's ability to invest in new generation.
Contact and ECNZ are both state-owned and compete with each other in the new market.
Recently the Paris-based International Energy Agency has suggested that the government consider further break-up of ECNZ to encourage greater competition in the wholesale electricity market.
Energy Minister Max Bradford, speaking to industry officials on Wednesday, said ECNZ was clearly frustrated by the constraints on new investment that the break-up agreement imposed upon it.

Bradford went on to say that it was important that competition was present in both the demand and supply ends of the electricity market. "The measures that we plan to implement, we believe will do that."

ECNZ has recently argued strenuously against any further break up of the corporation. Among earlier proposals for the break up of ECNZ was a three-way split that would have seen eight small hydro stations, now earmarked for sale, sold as one business.
Bradford said that the sale of those hydro stations was still Coalition government policy.
